subject.title: [Enhancement] Agent Tool Execution Safety: Forward Abort Signals to Before-Tool Hooks and Add Bounded Execution Timeouts

question: Should `before_tool_call` plugins receive a cancellable signal and should client/runtime hook failures share one structured outcome, while retaining the existing timeout owners?
rationale: Current main bounds hook admission but explicitly does not cancel plugin work; exposing cancellation and changing client terminal behavior affect plugin and agent-runtime contracts, while a universal tool deadline adds separate configuration policy.

options.title: Split lifecycle fix
options.body: Add signal-aware hook semantics and align client/runtime error handling without adding a new universal tool timeout layer.

options.title: Design unified deadlines
options.body: Specify cancellation plus a global per-tool default and override hierarchy across hooks, runtime tools, and client delegation.

options.title: Retain current contracts
options.body: Keep admission-only hook timeouts and the existing client/runtime error distinction, documenting the limitation.

recommendation.title: Split lifecycle fix
recommendation.body: Add signal-aware hook semantics and align client/runtime error handling without adding a new universal tool timeout layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent durable-approvals work owns the signal-aware pre-tool lifecycle and public hook documentation most directly.
